title: Noor & Celeste

redChapters.caseName: The Partner Who Always Covered for Me

description: Noor Haddad has spent three months believing she's losing her grip: missed tastings, cancelled orders, staff who won't meet her eye. Her business partner Celeste has covered for her every time. Tonight Celeste's phone is sitting on the bakery counter, and Noor finally wants to know what her partner really thinks of her.

questions.question:
I keep thinking I'm losing it, so let's start small.
A few weeks ago I opened alone at five. Two hundred croissants, just me and the radio.
She swears she lined someone up to come in with me. I don't remember any name.
Who was supposed to cover that shift with me?
questions.hint: Check her Messages.
questions.revealGuide:
Open Messages and go to the conversation with Ezra.
Read back a few weeks: Celeste asks him to open with Noor at 5 AM and he says yes.
That same evening she tells him to take the morning off because 'Noor wants to do it solo'.
Why: Ezra was the one booked to cover the shift, and Celeste cancelled him herself.

questions.question:
So she did ask someone, and I still ended up alone. 😔
Last week we ran out of flour mid-bake. Forty loaves short and a line out the door.
She handles every order. I just know the bags stopped coming.
Which supplier dropped us?
questions.hint: Look through her Mail inbox.
questions.revealGuide:
Open Mail and stay in the Inbox.
There are two flour suppliers. Fernhill Flour Co. only sends normal delivery notices.
Open 'Standing order SO-2208 cancelled' from Millrace Grain.
Why: Millrace Grain confirmed the bread flour standing order was cancelled.

questions.question:
I couldn't pick that company out of a lineup.
She says it went through on my login. I'm in bed by nine and up at 3:40, every night for five years.
What time did that cancellation actually go through?
questions.hint: Check the open tabs in Safari.
questions.revealGuide:
Open Safari and show all tabs.
Skip the Fernhill and Cascade Sugar order pages and open 'Millrace Grain · Wholesale Portal — Order Cancelled'.
Read the 'Submitted' line: 2:14 AM PT.
Why: the order was cancelled at 2:14 AM, while Noor was asleep.

questions.question:
That's the middle of the night. I was asleep. I know I was. 😤
Then there's the Whitcomb wedding tasting. She told me three o'clock. I got there at two-thirty with samples and they'd already left.
What time was it actually booked for?
questions.hint: Look at past events in her Calendar.
questions.revealGuide:
Open Calendar and go back to past events.
There are several tastings. Open 'Tasting — Whitcomb wedding' (the others are the Abernathy 60th and Rosewood Market catering).
The event starts at 11:00 AM. Priya's confirmation in Mail also says 'See you at 11!'.
Why: the tasting was booked for 11:00 AM, but Celeste told Noor 3.

questions.question:
So the tasting I 'missed' was never mine to miss.
Now the staff go quiet when I walk in. Someone's saying I screamed at them in the walk-in.

Who's been saying that?
questions.hint: Check her WhatsApp chats with the bakery staff.

Scroll up past the shift swaps, the pastry-case photos and the grinder complaints.

Mari writes: 'Noor screamed at me in the walk-in today. I'm not doing mornings alone with her anymore.'
Why: Mari (Marisol Vega) is the staff member saying Noor screamed at her.

questions.question:
She was my first hire. I taught her to laminate dough. 🥲

She writes: 'Please keep this between us. She's adjusting to new medication and it's been hard on her.'
Why: Celeste told Mari that Noor is on new medication.

questions.question:
I don't take anything. Not even for my bad wrist.
Every slip these past months, she was right there fixing it, telling me not to worry.
She's been keeping score, hasn't she.
How many of my so-called bad days has she counted?

Why: there are 9 entries, so Celeste has logged 9 'bad days'.

questions.question:

Nobody keeps score like that just for themselves.

The recipient is Garrett Lowe <glowe@loweostby.law>.
Why: Celeste is sending the log to Garrett Lowe.

Why: Celeste is building her case on the Incapacity clause.

Why: Martin Haddad, Noor's ex-husband, is behind MH Ventures.

questions.question:
Of course it's him. Of course. 💔
Two years since the divorce and he still can't stand that I walked away with the one thing he couldn't take.

questions.hint: Match a phone number from Mail to a WhatsApp chat.
questions.revealGuide:

Why: they call the plan Starter.

questions.question:

questions.hint: Open Photoshop and use Unblur.

Why: Celeste made a fake Sertraline label in Noor's name.

questions.question:

questions.hint: Look in Notes, WhatsApp and Phone.
questions.revealGuide:
In WhatsApp chat 'M.', find his message telling her to lock the meeting plan with Noor's birthday, month and day, four digits.
Open Phone → Contacts → 'Noor 🥖'. Her birthday is March 2, 1983, so the code is 0302.
In Notes, unlock the note 'Sit-down' with 0302.
Why: the note says 'Bring Rana. N listens to her', so she is bringing Rana, Noor's sister.

questions.question:

questions.hint: Check the newest emails in Mail.

Open 'Paperwork for the sit-down'. Ignore his separate 'Draft Incapacity Notice (fallback only)' email.
The attachment 'Voluntary_Withdrawal_Agreement_Haddad_v3.pdf' and the body name the Voluntary Withdrawal Agreement.
Why: Celeste wants Noor to sign a Voluntary Withdrawal Agreement.

textSuccess:
Every "don't worry, I've got it." Every hug. Every time she brought me tea while I cried about a mistake she'd made for me.

I thought I was going crazy. I was ready to hand her the keys and thank her for being so patient with me.

And Martin. Two years after the divorce, he still found a way back into my kitchen. Through the one person I'd have trusted with my life.

I'm calling Rana tonight, before Celeste gets to her. Then a lawyer of my own.

The ovens go on at four. I'll be there. It's still my bakery.

onboardingContent.text: I'm Noor. Head baker at Proof & Crumb in Portland. Four a.m., every day, for five years. Lately I keep making mistakes I can't remember making, and I'm scared it's me.
Celeste Moreau is my business partner. She runs the front and the books; I run the ovens. Every time I slipped this summer, she covered for me. Smiled, fixed it, told me not to worry.
She left her phone at the shop tonight. I've never once looked at it. But the staff go quiet when I walk in now, and I need to know what she really thinks of me.
My divorce nearly broke me. This bakery is what I rebuilt from it. Help me go through her phone, one question at a time. She'll be back for it at six.

safariTabs.content:
# Can an LLC member be forced out in Oregon?

**Short answer:** it depends on your operating agreement.

---

In Oregon, whether a member can be removed or bought out is mostly governed by what the members agreed to in writing. If the operating agreement has a buyout or expulsion provision, that provision controls. If it is silent, the default rules in the state's LLC statute apply.

### What to check

1. Does the agreement define when a member can be bought out?
2. How is the price set?
3. Is there a notice or cure period?

*This is general information, not legal advice. Talk to a licensed attorney.*

safariTabs.title: Avalanche vs. Snowball: Which Credit Card Payoff Method Works?
safariTabs.content:
# Avalanche vs. Snowball
## Paying off credit card debt

---

**Debt avalanche:** Pay minimums on everything, then throw every extra dollar at the card with the **highest APR**. Saves the most interest.

**Debt snowball:** Pay off the **smallest balance** first for quick wins and motivation.

### Quick comparison
| | Avalanche | Snowball |
|---|---|---|
| Interest saved | Most | Less |
| Motivation | Slower | Faster |
| Best for | Disciplined budgeters | People who need momentum |

### Other options
- **Balance transfer cards:** 0% intro APR for 15–21 months, usually a 3–5% fee
- **Personal consolidation loan:** one fixed payment, often lower rate
- Call your issuer and ask for a lower APR; it works more often than you'd think

> Tip: Automate the minimum, then schedule a second payment the day after payday.

[Use the payoff calculator](#)

## 12. Transfers

No Member may sell, assign or pledge any part of their membership interest without the written consent of the other Member, except as provided in this Agreement.

## 13. Right of First Refusal

If a Member receives a bona fide offer for their interest from a third party, the other Member has thirty (30) days to match the offer before any transfer may close.

## 14.1 Death of a Member

On the death of a Member, the estate may elect to sell the interest to the remaining Member at appraised fair market value.

## 14.2 Dissolution

The Company may be dissolved by the written agreement of both Members, or by court order. Proceeds are divided equally after debts are paid.

## 14.3 Incapacity of a Member

If a Member is unable to perform duties for a period exceeding ninety (90) days, the remaining Member may give written notice and purchase the interest of the incapacitated Member at sixty percent (60%) of appraised fair market value. Fair market value shall be set by an independent business appraiser chosen by the remaining Member.

## 15. Non-Compete

For two (2) years after leaving the Company, a withdrawing Member shall not open or operate a retail bakery within ten (10) miles of the Company's location.
